absent: Locking, concurrency and ordering rules for routing, irqfd, ioeventfd, device and VCPU controls
State machines for VCPU execution, MP states, interrupts, nested state, PIT and device lifecycle
Error codes, permission checks and validation of counts, flags, addresses and reserved fields
Runtime semantics and side effects of capabilities 228 through 251 beyond numeric assignment
Register index assignments, MSR and CPUID filter matching behavior and PMU filter semantics
Memory encryption subcommands, Xen attribute layouts and s390 operation detailed effects

findings.text: The numeric codes for extended capabilities are as follows: KVM_CAP_ARM_EAGER_SPLIT_CHUNK_SIZE is 228, KVM_CAP_ARM_SUPPORTED_BLOCK_SIZES is 229, KVM_CAP_ARM_SUPPORTED_REG_MASK_RANGES is 230, KVM_CAP_USER_MEMORY2 is 231, KVM_CAP_MEMORY_FAULT_INFO is 232, KVM_CAP_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTES is 233, KVM_CAP_GUEST_MEMFD is 234, KVM_CAP_VM_TYPES is 235, KVM_CAP_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY is 236, KVM_CAP_X86_APIC_BUS_CYCLES_NS is 237, KVM_CAP_X86_GUEST_MODE is 238, KVM_CAP_ARM_WRITABLE_IMP_ID_REGS is 239, KVM_CAP_ARM_EL2 is 240, KVM_CAP_ARM_EL2_E2H0 is 241, KVM_CAP_RISCV_MP_STATE_RESET is 242, KVM_CAP_ARM_CACHEABLE_PFNMAP_SUPPORTED is 243, KVM_CAP_GUEST_MEMFD_FLAGS is 244, KVM_CAP_ARM_SEA_TO_USER is 245, KVM_CAP_S390_USER_OPEREXEC is 246, KVM_CAP_S390_KEYOP is 247, KVM_CAP_S390_VSIE_ESAMODE is 248, KVM_CAP_S390_HPAGE_2G is 249, KVM_CAP_PPC_COMPAT_CAPS is 250, KVM_CAP_ARM_PMU_V3_STRICT is 251.

The five interrupt routing payload containers are kvm_irq_routing_irqchip and kvm_irq_routing_msi and kvm_irq_routing_s390_adapter and kvm_irq_routing_hv_sint and kvm_irq_routing_xen_evtchn. The first pairs a controller number with a pin number. The second pairs split address words with a data word and a final word used either as reserved space or as a device identifier. The third uses two 64 bit addresses with matching offsets plus an adapter number. The fourth pairs a processor index with a synthetic vector number. The fifth groups a port number with a processor index and a priority value.

The containers kvm_irq_routing_entry and kvm_irq_routing model one mapping and a variable length table. The table header holds a count and flags followed by a flexible trailing array of mappings. Each mapping holds a global interrupt number and a type selector and flags and reserved space, followed by a union that can hold any one of the five payload shapes or eight reserved words for future growth.

Routing type selectors are KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_IRQCHIP is 1 and KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_MSI is 2 and KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_S390_ADAPTER is 3 and KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_HV_SINT is 4 and KVM_IRQ_ROUTING_XEN_EVTCHN is 5. Xen two level priority is represented by all 32 bits set. Irqfd option bits are KVM_IRQFD_FLAG_DEASSIGN is bit 0 and KVM_IRQFD_FLAG_RESAMPLE is bit 1.

The container kvm_irqfd binds an event file descriptor to a global interrupt number with option bits and an optional resample descriptor plus padding for alignment. The container kvm_clock_data exchanges guest clock and realtime and host TSC values with a flags word and reserved words. The container kvm_config_tlb passes opaque parameters and an array address with a table type and length. The container kvm_dirty_tlb passes a bitmap address with a dirty count.
Clock validity markers are KVM_CLOCK_TSC_STABLE is 2 and KVM_CLOCK_REALTIME is bit 2 and KVM_CLOCK_HOST_TSC is bit 3. Book E table types are KVM_MMU_FSL_BOOKE_NOHV is 0 and KVM_MMU_FSL_BOOKE_HV is 1.

Architecture selection occupies the top byte of each 64 bit register identifier. Values are KVM_REG_ARCH_MASK is 0xff00000000000000 and KVM_REG_GENERIC is 0 and KVM_REG_PPC is 0x1000000000000000 and KVM_REG_X86 is 0x2000000000000000 and KVM_REG_IA64 is 0x3000000000000000 and KVM_REG_ARM is 0x4000000000000000 and KVM_REG_S390 is 0x5000000000000000 and KVM_REG_ARM64 is 0x6000000000000000 and KVM_REG_MIPS is 0x7000000000000000 and KVM_REG_RISCV is 0x8000000000000000 and KVM_REG_LOONGARCH is 0x9000000000000000.

Register size is encoded in bits 52 to 55 with KVM_REG_SIZE_SHIFT is 52 and KVM_REG_SIZE_MASK is 0x00f0000000000000. The decoded size is two raised to the extracted field, giving one byte through 2048 bytes. Encoded values are KVM_REG_SIZE_U8 is 0 and KVM_REG_SIZE_U16 is 0x0010000000000000 and KVM_REG_SIZE_U32 is 0x0020000000000000 and KVM_REG_SIZE_U64 is 0x0030000000000000 and KVM_REG_SIZE_U128 is 0x0040000000000000 and KVM_REG_SIZE_U256 is 0x0050000000000000 and KVM_REG_SIZE_U512 is 0x0060000000000000 and KVM_REG_SIZE_U1024 is 0x0070000000000000 and KVM_REG_SIZE_U2048 is 0x0080000000000000.

The container kvm_reg_list holds a 64 bit count followed by a flexible array of register identifiers. The container kvm_one_reg pairs one identifier with a userspace address for the value. The container kvm_msi holds split address words with data and flags and a device identifier plus padding. The container kvm_arm_device_addr pairs a device identifier with an address.

The container kvm_create_device carries a type selector with an output file descriptor and creation flags. The container kvm_device_attr carries flags with a group number and attribute code plus a userspace data address. The container kvm_vfio_spapr_tce pairs two file descriptors for group and table. The container kvm_s390_keyop carries a guest address with a key byte and operation byte plus padding. The container kvm_enc_region pairs an address with a size for encryption registration.

Probing uses KVM_CREATE_DEVICE_TEST is 1. VFIO file handling uses KVM_DEV_VFIO_FILE is 1 and KVM_DEV_VFIO_FILE_ADD is 1 and KVM_DEV_VFIO_FILE_DEL is 2, with group identifiers aliasing the same values and KVM_DEV_VFIO_GROUP_SET_SPAPR_TCE is 3. Device types are KVM_DEV_TYPE_FSL_MPIC_20 is 1 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_FSL_MPIC_42 is 2 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_XICS is 3 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_VFIO is 4 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V2 is 5 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_FLIC is 6 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V3 is 7 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_ITS is 8 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_XIVE is 9 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_PV_TIME is 10 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_RISCV_AIA is 11 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_LOONGARCH_IPI is 12 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_LOONGARCH_EIOINTC is 13 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_LOONGARCH_PCHPIC is 14 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_LOONGARCH_DMSINTC is 15 and KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V5 is 16. Key operations are KVM_S390_KEYOP_ISKE is 1 and KVM_S390_KEYOP_RRBE is 2 and KVM_S390_KEYOP_SSKE is 3. MSI identifier validity is KVM_MSI_VALID_DEVID is bit 0.

Machine scoped memory and processor controls are KVM_CREATE_VCPU is 0x41 and KVM_GET_DIRTY_LOG is 0x42 and KVM_SET_NR_MMU_PAGES is 0x44 and KVM_GET_NR_MMU_PAGES is 0x45 and KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION is 0x46 and KVM_SET_TSS_ADDR is 0x47 and KVM_SET_IDENTITY_MAP_ADDR is 0x48 and KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION2 is 0x49 and KVM_CLEAR_DIRTY_LOG is 0xc0. Associated payloads are dirty log, clear log, first and second generation user memory descriptors and a 64 bit address, with the 0x45 query noted as deprecated.

Payloads use irq level, irqchip, pit state, coalesced zone, routing, irqfd, pit config, ioeventfd, xen config, clock data, pit state2, create device and device attr.

Processor event and debug controls are KVM_GET_MP_STATE is 0x98 and KVM_SET_MP_STATE is 0x99 and KVM_NMI is 0x9a and KVM_SET_GUEST_DEBUG is 0x9b and KVM_X86_SETUP_MCE is 0x9c and KVM_X86_GET_MCE_CAP_SUPPORTED is 0x9d and KVM_X86_SET_MCE is 0x9e and KVM_GET_VCPU_EVENTS is 0x9f and KVM_SET_VCPU_EVENTS is 0xa0 and KVM_GET_DEBUGREGS is 0xa1 and KVM_SET_DEBUGREGS is 0xa2 and KVM_ENABLE_CAP is 0xa3 and KVM_GET_ONE_REG is 0xab and KVM_SET_ONE_REG is 0xac and KVM_KVMCLOCK_CTRL is 0xad and KVM_GET_REG_LIST is 0xb0 and KVM_SMI is 0xb7 and KVM_SIGNAL_MSI is 0xa5 and KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ is 0xa2 and KVM_GET_TSC_KHZ is 0xa3. Filtering, encryption, nesting and Xen controls are KVM_SET_PMU_EVENT_FILTER is 0xb2 and KVM_X86_SET_MSR_FILTER is 0xc6 and KVM_RESET_DIRTY_RINGS is 0xc7 and KVM_MEMORY_ENCRYPT_OP is 0xba and KVM_MEMORY_ENCRYPT_REG_REGION is 0xbb and KVM_MEMORY_ENCRYPT_UNREG_REGION is 0xbc and KVM_HYPERV_EVENTFD is 0xbd and KVM_GET_NESTED_STATE is 0xbe and KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE is 0xbf and KVM_DIRTY_TLB is 0xaa and KVM_XEN_HVM_GET_ATTR is 0xc8 and KVM_XEN_HVM_SET_ATTR is 0xc9 and KVM_XEN_VCPU_GET_ATTR is 0xca and KVM_XEN_VCPU_SET_ATTR is 0xcb and KVM_XEN_HVM_EVTCHN_SEND is 0xd0. Payloads use PMU filter, MSR filter, unsigned long subcommand, encryption region, hyperv eventfd, nested state, dirty TLB, Xen host and processor attributes and Xen event channel routing.

Payloads use UCAS mapping, unsigned long fault and status addresses, key operation, interrupt, program status word, memory operation, storage keys, interrupt state, migration access log and protected virtualization command.

PPC machine controls are KVM_PPC_GET_PVINFO is 0xa1 and KVM_PPC_GET_SMMU_INFO is 0xa6 and KVM_PPC_ALLOCATE_HTAB is 0xa7 and KVM_CREATE_SPAPR_TCE is 0xa8 and KVM_CREATE_SPAPR_TCE_64 is 0xa8 and KVM_ALLOCATE_RMA is 0xa9 and KVM_PPC_GET_HTAB_FD is 0xaa and KVM_PPC_RTAS_DEFINE_TOKEN is 0xac and KVM_PPC_RESIZE_HPT_PREPARE is 0xad and KVM_PPC_RESIZE_HPT_COMMIT is 0xae and KVM_PPC_CONFIGURE_V3_MMU is 0xaf and KVM_PPC_GET_RMMU_INFO is 0xb0 and KVM_PPC_GET_CPU_CHAR is 0xb1 and KVM_PPC_SVM_OFF is 0xb3 and KVM_PPC_GET_COMPAT_CAPS is 0xb8. Payloads use paravirtual info, SMMU info, a 32 bit word, two generations of SPAPR TCE descriptors, RMA description, HTAB file descriptor, RTAS token arguments, hash page table resize descriptors, MMU configuration, RMMU info and CPU characteristics.

ARM controls are KVM_ARM_SET_DEVICE_ADDR is 0xab and KVM_ARM_MTE_COPY_TAGS is 0xb4 and KVM_ARM_SET_COUNTER_OFFSET is 0xb5 and KVM_ARM_GET_REG_WRITABLE_MASKS is 0xb6 and KVM_ARM_VCPU_INIT is 0xae and KVM_ARM_PREFERRED_TARGET is 0xaf and KVM_ARM_VCPU_FINALIZE is 0xc2. Payloads use device address, MTE tag copy descriptor, counter offset, writable mask range, VCPU init descriptor and a plain integer for finalization.

Command numbers repeat across file descriptor kinds and architectures, so dispatch must consider the target object and not the number alone. Examples are 0x67 shared by line status and coalesced registration, 0xa8 shared by two SPAPR TCE generations, 0x9f and 0xa0 and 0xa1 and 0xa2 and 0xa3 and 0xaa through 0xb6 and 0xb8 reused between machine, processor and architecture handlers, and transfer direction varying between otherwise identical numbers.

Several payloads carry flexible trailing arrays or userspace addresses whose lengths live in separate fields, including routing tables, register lists, CPUID lists, MSR lists, nested state and device attributes. Callers must validate counts and addresses before access. Reserved and padding fields must be treated as zero on input and ignored on output unless a capability explicitly defines them, to preserve forward compatibility.

Dirty log options are KVM_DIRTY_LOG_MANUAL_PROTECT_ENABLE is bit 0 and KVM_DIRTY_LOG_INITIALLY_SET is bit 1 and KVM_DIRTY_LOG_PAGE_OFFSET is 0. S390 store status sentinels are KVM_S390_STORE_STATUS_NOADDR is all bits set and KVM_S390_STORE_STATUS_PREFIXED is all bits except the low bit clear pattern for minus two.

Register identifiers combine an architecture selector with a size code and a per register index, with the size field decoded as a power of two length. Routing entries select exactly one union member based on type, with unused tail words reserved. Counted flexible arrays are sized by their leading count fields and padding preserves alignment.
